Tesla and the Chinese push the market upwards — EV Share Jumps to 37% in Europe!

Thanks to a number of factors (new cheaper models, high gas prices, mass arrival of Chinese models, etc.), EVs are currently in high demand in Europe. Some 366,000 fully electric vehicles were registered in Europe in June, which is not only a 50% increase YoY, and the fastest growth rate this year, but also a new BEV record!

Overall, plugin vehicles were up 41% YoY, dragged down by plugin hybrids, which grew only 23%, thus placing June’s plugin share at 37%.

This difference in growth is also visible in the BEV vs. PHEV sales breakdown, with BEVs having 71% of all plugin sales in June. That placed their yearly average at 69%, which is their highest share since … 2012! Yep, like in China, it seems PHEVs are starting to lose the race to their BEVs counterparts…

With BEVs pulling the market upwards, the year-to-date share for BEVs is now at 23% (33% for PHEVs and BEVs combined), which is already higher than the 2025 final result (20% BEV share, 29% adding PHEVs). This is an encouraging sign if we want to be close to 100% PEV share by the mid-2030s.

Looking at the other fuels, there aren’t really major changes in trends in an overall market that grew 13% YoY in June to 1.4 million units. Plugless hybrids (HEVs) followed the overall trend by growing 17% YoY, to a market share of 35% — added to the 37% of plugins, that meant that in June, 72% of all cars sold in Europe had some kind of electrification, while pure ICEVs are … going down the drain.

Petrol was down 12% in June to 21% share, while diesel (-17% YoY) is now bordering on irrelevance, having just 6% of the market. A few more months, and probably i won’t even mention diesel anymore.

Looking at the best sellers in several size categories, the EV push is starting to get visible, while we are far from the EV domination we see in China, things have indeed moved on in Europe compared to last year.

Before, the only EVs that we saw on the overall podiums were Teslas. Now, the A-segment has the Leapmotor T03 as the overall 3rd placed model, closely followed by the Dacia Spring (5,676 units). Perhaps unsurprisingly. After all, the same happened in China before — it is in the city car category that EVs have the highest possibilities to have a fully 100% plugin podium sooner. First, the ICE competition is shrinking. Then, not only do we have the Leapmotor T03 already on the podium, but the new Renault Twingo is set to become a success, probably selling at higher levels than the Chinese EV. And … with a new Dacia Spring set to land soon, we have three competitive electric city cars ready to take over the podium.

Oh! And let’s not forget that a new Panda city car (Pandina?) is set to start in 2027, both in BEV and ICE versions. Speaking of which, adding an ICE version to the new Panda is another bad decision from Stellantis product planners, because while it is true that the 500e lost sales as years went by, it wasn’t because people wanted to go back to ICE cars, but because other, better, cheaper EVs started to land on the market, cannibalizing the 500e’s sales.

So, if I were them, I would make the new generation 100% BEV and keep on selling the old ICE generation for petrol diehards, as the “Panda Classic” or whatever.

Looking at the other segments, the B-segment is still ICE-heavy, with only the #3 Peugeot 208 having some degree of electrification (16% of sales are from the BEV version), the C-segment is a bit more electrified (#2 VW Golf is 14% PHEV, and #3 VW Tiguan is 32% PHEV), but it is the full size category where electrification is significant, with the #1 Mercedes E-Class having 36% of sales coming from the PHEV version, the #2 BMW 5 Series being 89% electrified (either with the BEV i5 or the PHEV versions), and the #3 BMW X5 having 28% of its sales coming from the PHEV version. And the 4th best selling model in this category was the fully electric Audi A6 e-tron, with 3,850 units.

So, A, D, and E segments have good electrification perspectives, but the all-important B and C segments, the most important in Europe, are the laggards.

Looking at the best selling EV models, the big news this month was Tesla winning 1st and 2nd place. BYD had 3rd place to itself thanks to the Atto 2 (BYD Yuan Up in Euro-spec). Here’s a more detailed analysis of the top 5 EVs this month:

#1 Tesla Model Y — Tesla’s midsize crossover is back in the driver’s seat thanks to 34,480 registrations in June, which represented a particularly strong high tide. Deliveries jumped 43% YoY and led to the nameplate’s best result since March 2023. And there’s still no Model Y L helping the brand along…. Such a high number of deliveries meant that Tesla’s midsizer was the #1 model in the overall market, beating the #2 Dacia Sandero by a sizeable 9,000 units. The crossover was the overall best seller across a number of European markets in June — it was #1 in the United Kingdom, Iceland, the Netherlands, Switzerland, Denmark and Norway. With Model Y prices starting at €40,000, and after six years on the market, the crossover still offers an appealing package. Currently, you buy a Tesla with your wallet/head, not your heart. Which is exactly the kind of buyer that is now searching for EVs. Many of these people simply want to lower their running costs by switching from ICEVs to BEVs. (Also, it’s why they are so popular with Ubers and such.)

#2 Tesla Model 3 — Tesla’s sedan was 2nd in June thanks to 18,028 registrations, a significant 67% increase YoY that allowed it to be 7th in the overall European market. Benefiting from the same tailwinds as the Model Y (mass delivery of the standard version, a surge in EV demand), the 10-year-old sedan is running along. It has a lot of demand now that price-conscious buyers are in the market and its prices, starting around €35,000, place it, a midsize sedan, in competition with models one segment below, compact hatchbacks. While the heart of the midsize car market is probably lost for the Model 3, a new segment of buyers, somewhere between the C and D segments, is giving it a second wind. As of this moment, it seems Tesla’s sedan could recover its podium position in 2026 … which is no mean feat for a 10-year-old model wearing a body type (sedan) not popular in Europe.

#3 BYD Atto 2 (BEV+PHEV) — The Chinese SUV hit another record performance last month, 13,100 registrations, mostly thanks to the new PHEV version. Why so popular in Europe? Besides not having real competition in the small PHEV category, the top range version has a 18 kWh battery, providing a usable range (90 km/56 mi). Additionally, it has increasingly important vehicle-to-load (V2L) capability. With the upcoming Dolphin G PHEV small hatchback using the same powertrain, expect the Shenzhen make to have another representative on the European table soon, especially considering that the new hatchback will be made in Hungary.

#4 BMW iX1/X1 PHEV — The German twins are in cruise control, winning another top 5 presence in June thanks to 11,778 registrations. Benefitting from favorable lease rates to help things along, the BMW crossovers are the brand’s bread and butter models, at least until the Neue Klasse models (i3 and iX3) get up to full speed. With a deep refresh coming to BMW’s compact models later this year, promising to transform them into baby Neue Klasse vehicles, expect both, but the iX1 in particular, to upgrade their specs. That will make them more interesting than the current versions and allow the Bavarian brand to keep its compact models as podium material.

#5 Renault 5 (including Alpine A290) — Renault’s star player delivered 10,785 sales in June, with the iconic hatchback increasing its sales year on year by 38%, thus backing previous optimistic statements from their representatives. The truth is that the French manufacturer has done its homework, and while others are scrambling with what to do next, Renault is now reaping the profits of its EV strategy. Sure, no matter how attractive the 5 is, the truth is that in 2026, its space in the market will be squeezed, not only by external competition like VW’s own take on the R5 formula, the ID.Polo, but also by internal competition, with the equally cute new Twingo potentially stealing sales from below. That is why Renault is taking a page from its Chinese counterparts and will upgrade its R5 and R4 in a few months with more efficient motors and LFP batteries, because cute design can only take you so far (just look at the Fiat 500e). The real factor to make the French twins true volume models over the years is meeting  constantly evolving buyer expectations — regarding specs, value for money, and pricing.

Outside the top 5, there were a number of highlights to mention.

Starting with BMW, we have another record result from the new BMW iX3 (in 9th place with 8,439 registrations). One wonders if the midsize SUV has already reached its cruising speed or there will be even higher volume months ahead. Regardless of what might happen to the iX3, I am now curious about the production ramp-up of the upcoming BMW i3. Will the new midsize sedan also reach top 10 status?

In the Mercedes stable, its star player, the CLA EV, continued in near-record territory, having clocked 6,676 registrations, while the three-pointed-star brand continued to ramp up both the new GLB EV seven-seater and the GLC EV midsizer, with both now starting to reach significant volumes (3,622 units for the former, 3,116 for the latter).

Volvo also had a good month, with both the EX30 (16th, 5,585 registrations) and the XC60 PHEV (14th, 6,134 registrations) performing year-best results. This is a positive sign for the Swedes, as these good results happen at a time when many clients are waiting for deliveries of the much anticipated new EX60. Expect Volvo to have a positive second half of the year as the new electric SUV starts to be delivered in volume.

Finally, a reference is due for the return of the veteran Dacia Spring. Thanks to 5,676 registrations, its best result since October 2023, it returned to the table at #15. With a new generation coming soon, expect the Spring to once again become a regular feature on the table, as a more rugged-looking counterpart to the new Renault Twingo.

Outside the top 20, in such a strong month, there was plenty to talk about, with good news almost everywhere:

  • At Volkswagen Group, the Audi A6 e-tron scored 3,850 units, a new year best, close to beating the current full size category kings, the BMW i5/5-Series PHEV twins (3,933 units).
  • Ford saw its Puma small crossover reach a record 4,604 units, no doubt thanks to recent price adjustments and improvements.
  • Thanks to the new Touring version, Toyota saw the sales of the BZ4X reach a new high, 4,802 deliveries.
  • Besides the R5’s success, Renault saw positive results across the lineup, with the Scenic ending the month in 21st with 4,888 registrations, just 12 units below the #20 Kia EV3. The soon-to-be-refreshed Megane hit its best score in two years thanks to 3,231 registrations, no doubt a good omen for the refreshed version, all while the new Twingo continued to ramp up deliveries, registering 4,524 units in June alone. Will the friendly face of the Renault city car join the table in July? One thing is certain, the French carmaker had five BEVs (R4, R5, Twingo, Scenic, Megane) above the 3,000-unit threshold in June. Not bad, Renault, not bad….
  • Kia’s new baby, the EV2 small crossover, ramped up deliveries to reach 3,357 units in June, while Polestar saw its 4 thingy score 4,099 registrations, a new year best.
  • As for the Chinese OEMs, there’s also news to report. Leapmotor is expanding its success streak beyond the T03 city car, by pushing its B10 compact crossover to reach a record 3,542 registrations; and Xpeng’s G6 midsize SUV hit a record 3,177 registrations, a significant mark for the startup now that the all-important L3 compact crossover is a couple of months away from landing.

Looking at the 2026 ranking, the major change in the top positions was the three-position jump of the Tesla Model 3 into the runner-up spot. And with a higher than expected delivery peak, Tesla’s sedan managed even to (barely) remove the Skoda Elroq from the second place.

With the competition experiencing different kinds of headwinds in the second half od the year (the Skoda Elroq suffering from the competition of its smaller sibling Epiq, BMW compact crossovers going through a refresh later this year, the Renault 5 witnessing the landing of new small hatchbacks — the VW ID.Polo, Cupra Raval, etc.) and the BYD Atto 2 being too far away to be a real threat, all of a sudden the Model 3 seems to be the strongest candidate for the silver medal, won by it the last time in 2024.

Bring on the popcorn, because this looks to be fun!

As for the remaining changes, the BYD Atto 2 continued to rise, going up to 8th. BYD’s small crossover is set to become the brand’s best seller in Europe — although, the upcoming Dolphin G could steal some sales from it.

On the second half of the table, the Mercedes CLA EV and Leapmotor T03 climbed one position each, to #11 and #12, respectively, while the Audi Q6 was up to #17. It was a positive month for Volvo, with the XC60 PHEV going up to #14 while the small EX30 rejoined the table in 19th.

Also set to join the table soon is the #21 BMW iX3. With the midsize SUV riding high, and being only some 200 units below the Citroen e-C3, I wouldn’t be surprised if the hot new electric SUV from Bavaria replaced the French supermini in July….

A few notes regarding the overall manufacturer ranking — the winners are currently Tesla and the Chinese.

  • Tesla sales were up 51% YoY in June, allowing it to be 11th overall;
  • But the highlights regard Chinese OEMs, which doubled their share from 5% in June 2025 to their current 10%. The biggest volume players are #15 MG, up 49% YoY to 39,000 units; #16 BYD, up 147%(!), to 38,500 units; #27 Leapmotor, up 568%(!); #28 Omoda, up 178%; and … the interesting case of Jaecoo. Chery’s Temu Land Rover was 26th, a 202% improvement, with the Chinese brand now outselling the original Land Rover (by 14,000 units to 8,000), with the Brits now being only 30th in June AND seeing sales drop by 10% in that same month (while the overall market grew by a significant 13%)…. Yep, Land Rover is in trouble.

As for the plugin auto brand ranking, the leader, Volkswagen, remained in the lead, but it lost significant share (8.9%, down from 9.3% in May). Sure, it still holds a comfortable advantage over rising BYD (7.9%, up 0.1%), and its new small EVs (VW ID.Polo, ID.Tiguan, etc.), should help it recover sales, but…. Volkswagen cannot afford to miss any more chances. Or else the company will get BYD on its back. In its home market. And if you can’t win at home,…

BMW (7%) was displaced from the last place on the podium by a rising Tesla (7.1% share, up from 6.3% in May). It is interesting to see the difference in Tesla’s performance as a brand comparing 2026 to the three previous times that Tesla had a #1 plus #2 lead in the model table — in 2022, 2023, and 2024. In those years, Tesla got gold and silver in the model table and at the same time won the manufacturer titles.

Now, with the same #1 plus #2 lead in the model table, Tesla is only 3rd among manufacturers. And not by a lot…. So, what is the difference? Lineup depth. Tesla has the usual two best sellers. BMW has 11 models on sale in Europe. And BYD has 17….

In 5th we have Mercedes (5.8%, down from 5.9% in May). It held steady in the 5th position, actually gaining a little bit of distance over #6 Audi (5.5%, down from 5.7% in May).

Thanks to good results across the lineup, #8 Renault (4.9%, up 0.1%) is on the way up and could start to pose a threat to #7 Skoda (5,3%) soon.

Arranging things by automotive group, Volkswagen Group is firmly in the lead, but it has lost share, now at 24% share, a significant 0.8% drop. Still, with plenty of fresh metal coming soon, expect the German OEM to rebound soon.

There was a position change in the runner-up spot, with troubled Stellantis (8.3%, down from 8.6% in May) losing the silver medal position to BMW Group (8.6%, up 0.1%). The multinational OEM’s drops seem to have no end in sight, and it could even lose its podium position this year, as a rising BYD (7.9%) is now just 0.4% share behind Stellantis.

So … maybe now is the time for Stellantis management to wake up and smell the coffee?

Outside the top 5, #6 Geely is rising (6.9%, up from 6.7% in May), but for the time being, it is still far from #5 Hyundai–Kia (7.3%) threatening it.

With the midsize SUV riding high, and being only some 200 units below the Citroen e-C3, I wouldn’t be surprised if the hot new electric SUV from Bavaria replaced the French supermini in July…. A few notes regarding the overall manufacturer ranking — the winners are currently Tesla and the Chinese. Tesla sales were up 51% YoY in June, allowing it to be 11th overall; But the highlights regard Chinese OEMs, which doubled their share from 5% in June 2025 to their current 10%. The biggest volume players are #15 MG, up 49% YoY to 39,000 units; #16 BYD, up 147%(!), to 38,500 units; #27 Leapmotor, up 568%(!); #28 Omoda, up 178%; and … the interesting case of Jaecoo. Chery’s Temu Land Rover was 26th, a 202% improvement, with the Chinese brand now outselling the original Land Rover (by 14,000 units to 8,000), with the Brits now being only 30th in June AND seeing sales drop by 10% in that same month (while the overall market grew by a significant 13%)…. Yep, Land Rover is in trouble. As for the plugin auto brand ranking, the leader, Volkswagen, remained in the lead, but it lost significant share (8.9%, down from 9.3% in May). Sure, it still holds a comfortable advantage over rising BYD (7.9%, up 0.1%), and its new small EVs (VW ID.Polo, ID.Tiguan, etc.), should help it recover sales, but…. Volkswagen cannot afford to miss any more chances. Or else the company will get BYD on its back. In its home market. And if you can’t win at home,… BMW (7%) was displaced from the last place on the podium by a rising Tesla (7.1% share, up from 6.3% in May). It is interesting to see the difference in Tesla’s performance as a brand comparing 2026 to the three previous times that Tesla had a #1 plus #2 lead in the model table — in 2022, 2023, and 2024. In those years, Tesla got gold and silver in the model table and at the same time won the manufacturer titles. Now, with the same #1 plus #2 lead in the model table, Tesla is only 3rd among manufacturers. And not by a lot…. So, what is the difference? Lineup depth. Tesla has the usual two best sellers. BMW has 11 models on sale in Europe. And BYD has 17…. In 5th we have Mercedes (5.8%, down from 5.9% in May). It held steady in the 5th position, actually gaining a little bit of distance over #6 Audi (5.5%, down from 5.7% in May). Thanks to good results across the lineup, #8 Renault (4.9%, up 0.1%) is on the way up and could start to pose a threat to #7 Skoda (5,3%) soon. Arranging things by automotive group, Volkswagen Group is firmly in the lead, but it has lost share, now at 24% share, a significant 0.8% drop. Still, with plenty of fresh metal coming soon, expect the German OEM to rebound soon. There was a position change in the runner-up spot, with troubled Stellantis (8.3%, down from 8.6% in May) losing the silver medal position to BMW Group (8.6%, up 0.1%). The multinational OEM’s drops seem to have no end in sight, and it could even lose its podium position this year, as a rising BYD (7.9%) is now just 0.4% share behind Stellantis. So … maybe now is the time for Stellantis management to wake up and smell the coffee? Outside the top 5, #6 Geely is rising (6.9%, up from 6.7% in May), but for the time being, it is still far from #5 Hyundai–Kia (7.3%) threatening it. blocks.html_en: Tesla and the Chinese push the market upwards — EV Share Jumps to 37% in Europe!

sentences.en: Tesla and the Chinese push the market upwards — EV Share Jumps to 37% in Europe!
sentences.zh: 特斯拉和中国推动市场向上——欧洲电动汽车份额跃升至 37%！

blocks.html_en: Thanks to a number of factors (new cheaper models, high gas prices, mass arrival of Chinese models, etc.), EVs are currently in high demand in Europe. Some 366,000 fully electric vehicles were registered in Europe in June, which is not only a 50% increase YoY, and the fastest growth rate this year, but also a new BEV record!

sentences.en: Thanks to a number of factors (new cheaper models, high gas prices, mass arrival of Chinese models, etc.), EVs are currently in high demand in Europe.
sentences.zh: 由于多种因素（更便宜的新车型、高油价、中国车型的大量上市等），电动汽车目前在欧洲的需求量很大。

sentences.en: Some 366,000 fully electric vehicles were registered in Europe in June, which is not only a 50% increase YoY, and the fastest growth rate this year, but also a new BEV record!
sentences.zh: 6月份欧洲纯电动汽车注册量约36.6万辆，不仅同比增长50%，是今年以来最快的增长速度，而且还刷新了纯电动汽车的纪录！

blocks.html_en: Overall, plugin vehicles were up 41% YoY, dragged down by plugin hybrids, which grew only 23%, thus placing June’s plugin share at 37%.

sentences.en: Overall, plugin vehicles were up 41% YoY, dragged down by plugin hybrids, which grew only 23%, thus placing June’s plugin share at 37%.
sentences.zh: 总体而言，插电式混合动力汽车同比增长 41%，而插电式混合动力汽车仅增长 23%，因此 6 月份的插电式汽车份额为 37%。

blocks.html_en: This difference in growth is also visible in the BEV vs. PHEV sales breakdown, with BEVs having 71% of all plugin sales in June. That placed their yearly average at 69%, which is their highest share since … 2012! Yep, like in China, it seems PHEVs are starting to lose the race to their BEVs counterparts…

sentences.en: This difference in growth is also visible in the BEV vs. PHEV sales breakdown, with BEVs having 71% of all plugin sales in June.
sentences.zh: 这种增长差异在 BEV 与 PHEV 销量细分中也可见一斑，6 月份 BEV 占所有插件销量的 71%。

sentences.en: That placed their yearly average at 69%, which is their highest share since …
sentences.zh: 这使得他们的年平均比例达到 69%，这是自……以来的最高比例。

sentences.en: Yep, like in China, it seems PHEVs are starting to lose the race to their BEVs counterparts…
sentences.zh: 是的，就像在中国一样，插电式混合动力汽车似乎开始输给纯电动汽车……

blocks.html_en: With BEVs pulling the market upwards, the year-to-date share for BEVs is now at 23% (33% for PHEVs and BEVs combined), which is already higher than the 2025 final result (20% BEV share, 29% adding PHEVs). This is an encouraging sign if we want to be close to 100% PEV share by the mid-2030s.

sentences.en: With BEVs pulling the market upwards, the year-to-date share for BEVs is now at 23% (33% for PHEVs and BEVs combined), which is already higher than the 2025 final result (20% BEV share, 29% adding PHEVs).

sentences.en: This is an encouraging sign if we want to be close to 100% PEV share by the mid-2030s.
sentences.zh: 如果我们希望到 2030 年代中期实现接近 100% 的 PEV 份额，这是一个令人鼓舞的迹象。

blocks.html_en: Looking at the other fuels, there aren’t really major changes in trends in an overall market that grew 13% YoY in June to 1.4 million units. Plugless hybrids (HEVs) followed the overall trend by growing 17% YoY, to a market share of 35% — added to the 37% of plugins, that meant that in June, 72% of all cars sold in Europe had some kind of electrification, while pure ICEVs are … going down the drain.

sentences.en: going down the drain.
sentences.zh: 付诸东流。

blocks.html_en: Petrol was down 12% in June to 21% share, while diesel (-17% YoY) is now bordering on irrelevance, having just 6% of the market. A few more months, and probably i won’t even mention diesel anymore.

sentences.zh: 6 月份汽油的份额下降了 12%，至 21%，而柴油（同比-17%）现在几乎无关紧要，仅占 6% 的市场份额。

sentences.en: A few more months, and probably i won’t even mention diesel anymore.
sentences.zh: 再过几个月，我可能就不会再提柴油了。

blocks.html_en: Looking at the best sellers in several size categories, the EV push is starting to get visible, while we are far from the EV domination we see in China, things have indeed moved on in Europe compared to last year.

sentences.en: Looking at the best sellers in several size categories, the EV push is starting to get visible, while we are far from the EV domination we see in China, things have indeed moved on in Europe compared to last year.
sentences.zh: 看看几个尺寸类别的畅销产品，电动汽车的推动开始变得明显，虽然我们距离中国看到的电动汽车主导地位还很远，但与去年相比，欧洲的情况确实发生了变化。

blocks.html_en: Before, the only EVs that we saw on the overall podiums were Teslas. Now, the A-segment has the Leapmotor T03 as the overall 3rd placed model, closely followed by the Dacia Spring (5,676 units). Perhaps unsurprisingly. After all, the same happened in China before — it is in the city car category that EVs have the highest possibilities to have a fully 100% plugin podium sooner. First, the ICE competition is shrinking. Then, not only do we have the Leapmotor T03 already on the podium, but the new Renault Twingo is set to become a success, probably selling at higher levels than the Chinese EV. And … with a new Dacia Spring set to land soon, we have three competitive electric city cars ready to take over the podium.

sentences.zh: 之前，我们在整个领奖台上看到的唯一电动汽车是特斯拉。

blocks.html_en: #1 Tesla Model Y — Tesla’s midsize crossover is back in the driver’s seat thanks to 34,480 registrations in June, which represented a particularly strong high tide. Deliveries jumped 43% YoY and led to the nameplate’s best result since March 2023. And there’s still no Model Y L helping the brand along…. Such a high number of deliveries meant that Tesla’s midsizer was the #1 model in the overall market, beating the #2 Dacia Sandero by a sizeable 9,000 units. The crossover was the overall best seller across a number of European markets in June — it was #1 in the United Kingdom, Iceland, the Netherlands, Switzerland, Denmark and Norway. With Model Y prices starting at €40,000, and after six years on the market, the crossover still offers an appealing package. Currently, you buy a Tesla with your wallet/head, not your heart. Which is exactly the kind of buyer that is now searching for EVs. Many of these people simply want to lower their running costs by switching from ICEVs to BEVs. (Also, it’s why they are so popular with Ubers and such.)

It has a lot of demand now that price-conscious buyers are in the market and its prices, starting around €35,000, place it, a midsize sedan, in competition with models one segment below, compact hatchbacks. While the heart of the midsize car market is probably lost for the Model 3, a new segment of buyers, somewhere between the C and D segments, is giving it a second wind. As of this moment, it seems Tesla’s sedan could recover its podium position in 2026 … which is no mean feat for a 10-year-old model wearing a body type (sedan) not popular in Europe.

blocks.html_en: #5 Renault 5 (including Alpine A290) — Renault’s star player delivered 10,785 sales in June, with the iconic hatchback increasing its sales year on year by 38%, thus backing previous optimistic statements from their representatives. The truth is that the French manufacturer has done its homework, and while others are scrambling with what to do next, Renault is now reaping the profits of its EV strategy. Sure, no matter how attractive the 5 is, the truth is that in 2026, its space in the market will be squeezed, not only by external competition like VW’s own take on the R5 formula, the ID.Polo, but also by internal competition, with the equally cute new Twingo potentially stealing sales from below. That is why Renault is taking a page from its Chinese counterparts and will upgrade its R5 and R4 in a few months with more efficient motors and LFP batteries, because cute design can only take you so far (just look at the Fiat 500e). The real factor to make the French twins true volume models over the years is meeting  constantly evolving buyer expectations — regarding specs, value for money, and pricing.

特斯拉和中国推动市场向上——欧洲电动汽车份额跃升至 37%！

由于多种因素（更便宜的新车型、高油价、中国车型的大量上市等），电动汽车目前在欧洲的需求量很大。 6月份欧洲纯电动汽车注册量约36.6万辆，不仅同比增长50%，是今年以来最快的增长速度，而且还刷新了纯电动汽车的纪录！

总体而言，插电式混合动力汽车同比增长 41%，而插电式混合动力汽车仅增长 23%，因此 6 月份的插电式汽车份额为 37%。

这种增长差异在 BEV 与 PHEV 销量细分中也可见一斑，6 月份 BEV 占所有插件销量的 71%。 这使得他们的年平均比例达到 69%，这是自……以来的最高比例。 2012! 是的，就像在中国一样，插电式混合动力汽车似乎开始输给纯电动汽车……

随着纯电动汽车拉动市场向上，今年迄今为止纯电动汽车的份额现已达到 23%（插电式混合动力汽车和纯电动汽车合计为 33%），这已经高于 2025 年的最终结果（纯电动汽车份额为 20%，加上插电式混合动力汽车为 29%）。 如果我们希望到 2030 年代中期实现接近 100% 的 PEV 份额，这是一个令人鼓舞的迹象。

看看其他燃料，整个市场的趋势并没有真正发生重大变化，6 月份同比增长 13% 至 140 万辆。 无插电混合动力车 (HEV) 紧随整体趋势，同比增长 17%，市场份额达到 35%（加上 37% 的插电式混合动力车），这意味着 6 月份欧洲销售的所有汽车中有 72% 配备了某种电气化系统，而纯 ICEV 则…… 付诸东流。

6 月份汽油的份额下降了 12%，至 21%，而柴油（同比-17%）现在几乎无关紧要，仅占 6% 的市场份额。 再过几个月，我可能就不会再提柴油了。

看看几个尺寸类别的畅销产品，电动汽车的推动开始变得明显，虽然我们距离中国看到的电动汽车主导地位还很远，但与去年相比，欧洲的情况确实发生了变化。

之前，我们在整个领奖台上看到的唯一电动汽车是特斯拉。 目前，A级车中零跑T03位居第三，紧随其后的是达契亚Spring（5,676辆）。 也许并不奇怪。 毕竟，同样的情况之前在中国也发生过——在城市汽车类别中，电动汽车最有可能更快登上完全 100% 插电式领奖台。 首先，ICE竞争正在萎缩。 那么，不仅零跑T03已经登上领奖台，新款雷诺Twingo也将取得成功，其销量可能会高于中国电动汽车。 和 … 随着新款达契亚 Spring 即将上市，我们拥有三款具有竞争力的电动城市汽车，准备登上领奖台。

哦！ 我们不要忘记一辆新的熊猫城市汽车（Pandina？） 预计将于 2027 年推出，有 BEV 和 ICE 版本。 说到这里，在新款 Panda 上添加 ICE 版本是 Stellantis 产品规划人员的另一个错误决定，因为虽然 500e 的销量确实随着时间的推移而下降，但这并不是因为人们想回到 ICE 汽车，而是因为其他更好、更便宜的电动汽车开始登陆市场，蚕食了 500e 的销量。

所以，如果我是他们，我会制造新一代 100% BEV，并继续向汽油顽固分子销售旧的 ICE 一代，如“熊猫经典”或其他什么。

看看其他细分市场，B级车仍然以内燃机为主，只有#3标致208有一定程度的电气化（16%的销量来自纯电动版本），C级车的电动化程度更高一些（#2大众高尔夫为14%插电式混合动力，#3大众途观为32%插电式混合动力），但它是全尺寸车型，电气化很重要，其中排名第一的梅赛德斯 E 级轿车 36% 的销量来自插电式混合动力版本，排名第二的宝马 5 系的 89% 是电动化的（无论是 BEV i5 还是插电式混合动力版本），而排名第三的宝马 X5 的销量则有 28% 来自插电式混合动力版本。 该类别中第四畅销车型是全电动奥迪 A6 e-tron，销量为 3,850 辆。

因此，A、D和E细分市场具有良好的电气化前景，但最重要的B和C细分市场（欧洲最重要的）却是落后者。

纵观最畅销的电动汽车车型，本月的大新闻是特斯拉获得第一和第二名。 比亚迪凭借 Atto 2（欧洲规格的比亚迪元升级）获得第三名。 以下是本月排名前 5 名的电动汽车的更详细分析：

#1 特斯拉 Model Y——特斯拉的中型跨界车在 6 月份的注册量达到 34,480 辆，这代表着特别强劲的高潮，特斯拉的中型跨界车重新回到了驾驶座上。 交付量同比增长 43%，创下 2023 年 3 月以来的最佳业绩。 而且仍然没有 Model Y L 帮助该品牌前进...... 如此高的交付量意味着特斯拉的中型车成为整个市场排名第一的车型，以 9,000 辆的优势击败排名第二的 Dacia Sandero。 这款跨界车是 6 月份多个欧洲市场的整体最畅销产品，在英国、冰岛、荷兰、瑞士、丹麦和挪威排名第一。 Model Y 的起价为 40,000 欧元，上市六年后，这款跨界车仍然具有吸引力。 目前，你买特斯拉是用你的钱包/头脑，而不是你的心。 这正是现在正在寻找电动汽车的买家。 其中许多人只是想通过从 ICEV 转向 BEV 来降低运营成本。 （这也是为什么它们如此受 Uber 之类的欢迎。）

#2 特斯拉 Model 3 — 特斯拉的轿车在 6 月份排名第二，注册量为 18,028 辆，同比大幅增长 67%，在整个欧洲市场排名第七。 受益于与 Model Y 相同的顺风车（标准版的批量交付、电动汽车需求的激增），这款已有 10 年历史的轿车正在持续发展。 现在市场上对价格敏感的买家对它有很大的需求，其起价约为 35,000 欧元，是一款中型轿车，与低一级的紧凑型掀背车车型竞争。 虽然 Model 3 可能失去了中型汽车市场的核心，但介于 C 和 D 级之间的新买家群体正在给它带来重生。 截至目前，特斯拉的轿车似乎可以在 2026 年恢复领奖台位置…… 对于一个穿着欧洲不流行的车身类型（轿车）的 10 岁模特来说，这绝非易事。

#3 比亚迪 Atto 2（BEV+PHEV）——这款中国 SUV 上个月再创新高，注册量达到 13,100 辆，这主要归功于新的 PHEV 版本。 为何在欧洲如此受欢迎？ 除了在小型 PHEV 类别中没有真正的竞争外，顶级版本还配备 18 kWh 电池，提供可用范围（90 公里/56 英里）。 此外，它还具有越来越重要的车辆到负载 (V2L) 功能。 随着即将推出的使用相同动力系统的 Dolphin G PHEV 小型掀背车，预计深圳制造商很快就会在欧洲市场上再添一位代表，特别是考虑到新款掀背车将在匈牙利制造。

#4 BMW iX1/X1 PHEV — 这对德国双胞胎采用巡航控制系统，凭借 11,778 的注册量，在 6 月份再次跻身前五名。 得益于优惠的租赁利率，宝马跨界车成为了该品牌的主要车型，至少在 Neue Klasse 车型（i3 和 iX3）全速发展之前是这样。 今年晚些时候，宝马的紧凑型车型将进行深度更新，并承诺将其改造成 Neue Klasse 婴儿车，预计这两款车型，尤其是 iX1，都会升级其规格。 这将使它们比当前版本更有趣，并使巴伐利亚品牌能够保持其紧凑型车型作为领奖台材料。

#5 雷诺 5（包括 Alpine A290）——雷诺的明星车型 6 月份销量为 10,785 辆，这款标志性掀背车的销量同比增长了 38%，从而支持了其代表之前的乐观声明。 事实是，这家法国制造商已经做好了功课，当其他人都在忙着下一步该做什么时，雷诺现在正在收获其电动汽车战略的利润。 当然，无论 5 多么有吸引力，事实是，到 2026 年，它的市场空间将受到挤压，不仅受到大众自己的 R5 车型 ID.Polo 等外部竞争的挤压，而且还受到内部竞争的挤压，同样可爱的新款 Twingo 可能会从下面抢走销量。 这就是为什么雷诺效仿中国同行，将在几个月内升级其 R5 和 R4，配备更高效的电机和 LFP 电池，因为可爱的设计只能带你走这么远（看看菲亚特 500e）。 多年来，法国双胞胎真正量产的真正因素是满足不断变化的买家对规格、物有所值和定价的期望。

除了前 5 名之外，还有许多亮点值得一提。

从 BMW 开始，新款 BMW iX3 又创下了新纪录（以 8,439 辆注册量排名第 9）。 人们想知道这款中型 SUV 是否已经达到了巡航速度，或者未来几个月的销量还会更高。 不管 iX3 会发生什么，我现在对即将推出的 BMW i3 的产量增长感到好奇。 新款中型轿车是否也能进入前十名？

在梅赛德斯车队中，其明星车型 CLA EV 继续保持接近纪录的水平，注册量为 6,676 辆，而三尖明星品牌则继续增加新款 GLB EV 七座车和 GLC EV 中型车的销量，两者现在都开始达到可观的销量（前者为 3,622 辆，后者为 3,116 辆）。

沃尔沃本月表现也不错，EX30（第 16 名，注册量 5,585 辆）和 XC60 PHEV（第 14 名，注册量 6,134 辆）均取得了年度最佳成绩。 这对瑞典人来说是一个积极的信号，因为这些良好的业绩发生在许多客户正在等待备受期待的新款 EX60 交付之际。 随着新款电动 SUV 开始批量交付，预计沃尔沃下半年将取得积极进展。

最后，值得一提的是老牌达契亚Spring的回归。 凭借 5,676 名注册人数，这是自 2023 年 10 月以来的最佳成绩，它重返排行榜第 15 位。 随着新一代车型的即将推出，预计Spring将再次成为桌面上的常规特征，作为新款雷诺Twingo的外观更加坚固的对手。

在如此强劲的一个月里，在前 20 名之外，有很多值得谈论的事情，几乎到处都有好消息：

  • 在大众汽车集团，奥迪 A6 e-tron 获得了 3,850 辆的销量，创下了新年最佳成绩，接近击败当前全尺寸车型的王者——宝马 i5/5 系列 PHEV 双胞胎（3,933 辆）。
  • 福特的 Puma 小型跨界车销量达到创纪录的 4,604 辆，这无疑要归功于最近的价格调整和改进。
  • 得益于新的Touring版本，丰田BZ4X的销量再创新高，交付量达到4,802辆。
  • 除了 R5 的成功之外，雷诺的整个产品线也取得了积极的成果，截至 21 日，Scenic 的注册量为 4,888 辆，仅比 20 号起亚 EV3 少 12 辆。 即将更新的梅甘娜以 3,231 辆的注册量创下了两年来的最高成绩，这对更新版来说无疑是一个好兆头，而新款 Twingo 则继续增加交付量，仅 6 月份就注册了 4,524 辆。 雷诺城市汽车的友善面孔会在七月加入榜单吗？ 有一点是肯定的，这家法国汽车制造商有五款纯电动汽车（R4、R5、Twingo、Scenic、Megane）在 6 月份的销量超过了 3,000 辆。 不错，雷诺，不错……
  • 起亚的新宝贝 EV2 小型跨界车 6 月份的交付​​量猛增至 3,357 辆，而 Polestar 的 4 款车型注册量达到 4,099 辆，创下了新年最好成绩。
  • 至于中国整车厂，也有消息要报道。 零跑汽车正在将其成功势头扩大到T03城市轿车之外，其B10紧凑型跨界车的注册量达到创纪录的3,542辆；小鹏汽车的 G6 中型 SUV 注册量达到创纪录的 3,177 辆，这对于这家初创公司来说是一个重要的里程碑，因为最重要的 L3 紧凑型跨界车距离上市还有几个月的时间。

从2026年的排名来看，前几位的主要变化是特斯拉Model 3跃升三位，跃居亚军。 由于交付峰值高于预期，特斯拉的轿车甚至（勉强）将斯柯达 Elroq 从第二名的位置上挤了下来。

下半年竞争经历了不同的逆风（斯柯达Elroq遭受其较小兄弟Epiq的竞争，宝马紧凑型跨界车在今年晚些时候进行更新，雷诺5见证了新型小型掀背车的登陆 - 大众ID.Polo，Cupra Raval等）以及比亚迪Atto 2距离太远而无法构成真正的威胁，突然之间，Model 3似乎成为银奖的最强候选者上一次获得奖牌是在2024年。

带上爆米花，因为这看起来很有趣！

其余变化方面，比亚迪Atto 2继续上升，升至第8位。 比亚迪的小型跨界车将成为该品牌在欧洲最畅销的车型——不过，即将推出的Dolphin G可能会抢走该品牌的一些销量。

后半段，梅赛德斯CLA EV和零跑T03分别上升一位，分别升至第11位和第12位，奥迪Q6升至第17位。 对于沃尔沃来说，这是一个积极的月份，XC60 PHEV 上升至第 14 名，而小型 EX30 则重新上榜，排名第 19 位。

即将加入榜单的还有#21 BMW iX3。 随着这款中型 SUV 的发展势头强劲，且仅比雪铁龙 e-C3 低约 200 辆，如果这款来自巴伐利亚的热门新型电动 SUV 在 7 月份取代法国超迷你车，我不会感到惊讶……

关于制造商整体排名的一些注意事项——目前获胜者是特斯拉和中国。

  • 特斯拉 6 月份销量同比增长 51%，整体排名第 11 位；
  • 但最引人注目的是中国整车厂，其份额从 2025 年 6 月的 5% 翻了一番，达到目前的 10%。 销量最大的是#15 MG，同比增长 49% 至 39,000 辆； #16 比亚迪，增长 147%（！），达到 38,500 辆； #27 零跑汽车，上涨568%（！）； #28 Omoda，上涨 178%；和 … Jaecoo 的有趣案例。 奇瑞的 Temu Land Rover 排名第 26 位，提升了 202%，中国品牌现在的销量超过了原来的 Land Rover（14,000 辆，达到 8,000 辆），而英国品牌在 6 月份仅排名第 30 位，同月销量下降了 10%（而整体市场增长了 13%）…… 是的，路虎遇到了麻烦。

插电式汽车品牌排名中，领头羊大众仍保持领先，但份额大幅下滑（8.9%，低于5月份的9.3%）。 当然，与不断上涨的比亚迪（7.9％，上涨0.1％）相比，它仍然拥有明显的优势，而其新型小型电动汽车（大众ID.Polo、ID.Tiguan等）应该有助于其恢复销量，但是…… 大众汽车不能再错过任何机会。 否则该公司就会背上比亚迪的后盾。 在其本土市场。 如果你不能在主场获胜，...

宝马 (7%) 被排名最后的特斯拉 (7.1% 份额，高于 5 月份的 6.3%) 取代。 有趣的是，将 2026 年特斯拉作为一个品牌的表现与前三次（2022 年、2023 年和 2024 年）特斯拉在车型表中排名第一加第二的表现进行比较，发现了差异。 那些年，特斯拉在车型榜上获得了金奖和银奖，同时也赢得了制造商称号。

现在，特斯拉在车型表中同样排名第一加第二，在制造商中仅排名第三。 而且不是很多…… 那么，有什么区别呢？ 阵容深度。 特斯拉通常有两款畅销产品。 宝马在欧洲有 11 款车型在售。 而比亚迪有17个……

排名第五的是梅赛德斯（5.8%，低于 5 月份的 5.9%）。 它稳定在第五位，实际上比排名第六的奥迪（5.5%，低于 5 月份的 5.7%）有一点距离。

由于整个阵容都取得了良好的成绩，排名第八的雷诺（4.9%，上涨 0.1%）正在崛起，并可能很快开始对排名第七的斯柯达（5.3%）构成威胁。

从汽车集团来看，大众集团稳居领先地位，但份额有所下降，目前份额为24%，大幅下降0.8个百分点。 尽管如此，随着大量新金属即将上市，预计德国原始设备制造商将很快反弹。

亚军位置发生了变化，陷入困境的 Stellantis（8.3%，低于 5 月份的 8.6%）将银牌位置输给了宝马集团（8.6%，上升了 0.1%）。 这家跨国整车厂的下滑似乎没有尽头，今年甚至可能失去领奖台的位置，因为不断上升的比亚迪 (7.9%) 目前仅落后 Stellantis 0.4% 的份额。

所以 … 也许现在是 Stellantis 管理层醒来并闻到咖啡香味的时候了？

在前五名之外，排名第六的吉利正在上升（6.9%，高于 5 月份的 6.7%），但就目前而言，距离排名第五的现代起亚（7.3%）还很远。
